Contradiction. OPCODES.md 'What this does not cover' still says any account can reach the never-run MULMOD sites only in a pool it creates and that a wide amount cannot be settled. Cycle 38 showed the fee site in existing pools with settleable amounts, and cycle 39 (theme-never-run-sites-shared-balance cleared items) shows site B settles for about 2.9e10 wei in an own pool of shared currencies and pays from the shared balance on a wrong word. The theme's medium lead carries replacement wording; it should be applied by the merge step.

Contradiction of priority. theme-ethereum-binaries-storage-journal marks the evm2 journal lift from the reth v2.11.0 binary high. Ethereum blocks are accepted by a supermajority of geth, nethermind, besu and erigon nodes, so a reth-only journal fault forks reth nodes off and gives an ordinary account no lasting payout on the canonical chain. Under the threat model this is low for chain 1. The same evm2 journal matters where evm2 is the only client (Tempo, which pins rev 7c9f3b6, a different revision).

Contradiction of scale. F-105 is recorded with actor operator at medium, and its verifier kept medium, while SCHEMA.md places a loss or freeze that needs a sequencer at high. The verifier's reason (the L1 escape is closed only for positions holding about 17,000 dollars) is a size argument the scale does not provide for. The verifier also left the statement about the eight largest pools unverified.

Contradiction of numbers. stablecoin-l1 profile 5042 L3 gives the PoolManager's native USDC as about 2,430,783, its verifier read 2,443,346. Neither names the block. F-137's victim is the sender who named the PoolManager as mint recipient, which the verifier calls a user error outside the victim class; the finding still carries actor unprivileged and severity low.

leads.question: In the runtime of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json, every MULMOD that takes an operand from a PUSH literal in its own basic block is in the never-run set: modulus 2^128 at pc 22378 (Position copy, PUSH17 at 22359), modulus 10^6 at pc 22513 (fee copy, PUSH3 at 22508), modulus 2^96 at pc 22639 (site B, PUSH13 at 22624), and multiplicand 2^96 at pcs 20958, 22721 and 22763 (site D). The three MULMOD sites that the producers did run wide (22892, 22921, 23678) take every operand from the stack (critic disassembly). In the cycle 33 MegaETH validated-block census and the cycle 37 HyperEVM replica census, how many wide MULMOD executions in any contract had an operand pushed as a literal in the same basic block, split by literal value and by position (modulus or multiplicand)?
leads.why: A compiler that specialises constant operands lowers exactly these sites differently from the interpreter (the evm2 JIT lowers a power of two modulus to an AND, peephole.rs as cleared earlier; revmc main has const_fold.rs and peephole.rs passes). The 495,303 wide runs the theme cites in other contracts say nothing about this lowering unless their operands were literals too. A zero count means no evidence at all exists that the MegaETH or HyperEVM producer computes a literal-operand MULMOD right, and site B at pc 22639 pays out of the shared balance of currency1 on a word that is too small (theme-never-run-sites-shared-balance, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252, src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:69-71, src/PoolManager.sol:291-297).

leads.question: Does any contract on MegaETH or HyperEVM other than the PoolManager carry byte sequences identical to the PoolManager basic blocks of site B (pcs 22544 to 22660), donate (pcs 10223 to 10518) or the exact-output step (pcs 20618 to 20840), for example a second deployment of the 24,009 byte runtime or a v4 fork built with solc 0.8.26 via_ir at 44444444 runs, and did a mined transaction execute those blocks there? Search the code hashes seen in the cycle 33 and cycle 37 traces for the 64 byte windows around pcs 22639, 10491 and 20672.
leads.why: A per-contract compiler emits the same machine code for the same bytes and the same constant context, so a mined run of an identical block elsewhere is the only read-only substitute for the mined PoolManager transaction that the three high leads of the theme require. If no such contract exists, the leads can close only by a deployer canary before launch.

leads.question: Run the compiled PoolManager blocks that contain pc 22639 (site B), pcs 10491 and 10513 (donate fee growth) and the exact-output step through the shipped Monad 0.16.7 emitter with the cycle 39 attacker states: the site B pool built on 0xee8c0e9f1bffb4eb878d8f15f368a02a35481242 (tick spacing 32767, price at tick 851,941, position [851942, 884709], liquidity 2^96.5, exact-input oneForZero 1000) and donate(1, 1) in pool 0x3783b51e33900eb3. Do price, amounts and feeGrowthGlobal equal the interpreter answer (price after 249827439116968746553502782595956059949443474316, fee growth +43,133,901,828,545)?
leads.why: Monad validators all run the same native code, which RPC never runs, so a compiler fault on these inputs would be agreed by the quorum and would pay out of the shared balance (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252). Cycles 31 to 37 ran these blocks only on logged real states, which never hold the wide site B operands, and the harness to run them exists.

leads.question: Run the public stateless validator over every MegaETH block with a PoolManager log from 32,987,130 to head (33,048,029 at 05:50 UTC on 2026-11-28) and report, per pc of the never-run set (22378, 22513, 22639, 22721, 22763, 10491, 10513, 23924), whether it executed and with which operands.
leads.why: The validator re-executes producer blocks and checks the state root, so a validated block that ran a never-run pc is producer evidence. If an account has already driven site B or donate since the census, the question is settled; if a validated block disagreed it would show the fault.

leads.question: Are the journal, transient storage and storage handler source files of evm2 byte equal between rev 7c9f3b6 (Tempo v1.19.2) and rev 66687c1 (reth v2.11.0)? List every file that differs and say whether any difference touches tload, tstore, sload, sstore, checkpoint or revert.

leads.question: bor develop added keccakLoadOrCompute with a cache for variable-length inputs up to 8,192 bytes (core/vm/instructions.go, Config.keccakCache). Do bsc develop, ava-labs libevm main and celo op-geth master carry any new cache, memo or fused path in front of KECCAK256, MULMOD, SLOAD or TLOAD since the cycle 29 handler comparison, and does the bor cache compare the whole input and stay per EVM?
leads.why: Every mapping slot and every currency delta slot of the PoolManager is a keccak of a 64 byte input (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol, src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:325-347). A cache that returns another input's hash would write or read another account's delta or pool slot.

leads.question: The Circle Gateway minter address 0x2222222d7164433c4C09B0b0D809a9b52C04C205 has 163 bytes of code on these nine networks as well as Arc (critic eth_getCode on the networks.json endpoints, 2026-11-28; zero bytes on the other eleven). On each, does the minter accept any caller when destinationCaller is zero and mint USDC to the attested recipient without calling it, as Mints.sol lines 295-297 and 333-349 do on Arc, and has any Gateway mint named the PoolManager?
leads.why: That would extend F-137 (a relay executed by an ordinary account inside its own sync and settle and booked as its payment) from Arc to every network with Gateway. The loss falls on the sender who named the PoolManager, not on LPs, so it stays low.

leads.question: For F-137 on Arc, is the attestation for a pending Gateway mint retrievable by an account other than the requester (GET /v1/transfer/{id} without the requester's credentials, or a pending transaction feed on any Arc RPC), and is the victim in every such case a sender who chose the PoolManager as recipient?
leads.why: This is the one fact that moves F-137 from plausible to confirmed or refuted, and it decides whether the actor field and the victim class match the threat model.
